question: Design a broadband one-dimensional antireflection coating for a fused-silica substrate in air over 450-700 nm. The coating must use isotropic, practically depositable dielectric materials selected from MgF2, SiO2, Al2O3, Ta2O5, and TiO2. Let the system determine a reasonable material sequence and compare several fixed layer-count routes between 4 and 10 finite layers. Evaluate incidence angles of 0, 30, and 45 degrees for both TE and TM polarization. Use soft goals of mean reflectance at or below 0.8 percent and worst-case reflectance at or below 3 percent over the full wavelength-angle-polarization domain; also reward fewer layers and lower total physical thickness without treating diversity or exact target attainment as a hard gate. Verify all candidates with TMM, report the best-performance, most robust, and simplest physically valid designs, and analyze independent one-sigma thickness errors of 2 nm together with a common incidence-angle offset bounded by plus or minus 1 degree. If the exact optical goals conflict with layer count or robustness, return the best verified trade-offs and explain the limitation rather than declaring failure.
